Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Go-to-Market Enablement develops the capabilities that help Stripe’s customer-facing teams deliver greater value to users. We align expectations for role excellence, build practical learning experiences, and equip managers to reinforce new skills and behaviors.

Stripe’s Customer Success Managers are ongoing partners to some of our largest users after they begin using Stripe. They help users understand the health of their business on Stripe, address challenges, and identify opportunities to get more value from our products. Through regular business reviews and account engagement, they connect users’ priorities with how Stripe can support their business.

The Customer Success Enablement Business Partner will support these teams from onboarding through ongoing development, connecting global enablement programs with the priorities of Customer Success leaders, managers, and teams.

What you’ll do

You’ll serve as the strategic enablement partner to Customer Success leadership, helping identify the skills, knowledge, and practices that Customer Success Managers need to support their users effectively. You’ll translate those needs into a focused enablement roadmap and work with global program owners, Customer Success Operations, and subject matter experts to deliver it.

You’ll bring an understanding of customer success work and combine strategic partnership with hands-on execution. That includes shaping role-specific learning offerings, equipping managers to reinforce skills, and using data and feedback to evaluate what’s working. You’ll also make clear tradeoffs about priorities, protect the team’s time, and connect stakeholders with the right expertise across enablement.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with Customer Success leadership to define and execute an enablement strategy aligned with business priorities, role expectations, and performance needs
  • Shape onboarding and ongoing development for CSMs, building role-specific offerings and coordinating handoffs for ongoing administration and management
  • Build the governance, roadmaps, and operating rhythms needed to prioritize requests, manage dependencies, and deliver complex programs with consistency
  • Coordinate with Customer Success Operations, technical enablement, Product, and Marketing to prepare teams for evolving products, processes, tools, and user needs
  • Maintain an enablement roadmap, manage cross-functional dependencies, and communicate priorities, progress, and tradeoffs to leaders and stakeholders
  • Use conversation intelligence, learning and competency data, business indicators, and field feedback to identify needs and evaluate enablement effectiveness
  • Lead learning sessions and equip managers to reinforce skills through practice, coaching, assessment, and feedback

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in customer success, professional services, enablement, program management, or a related field supporting post-sales or customer-facing teams
  • Working knowledge of the customer success role, demonstrated through direct experience or close partnership with customer success teams
  • Experience leading complex, cross-functional programs, including setting priorities, managing dependencies, and coordinating execution
  • Experience partnering with senior stakeholders, communicating recommendations and tradeoffs, and translating business needs into practical programs, resources, or guidance
  • Experience using data and stakeholder feedback to identify performance needs, evaluate results, and improve programs or ways of working

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience designing or delivering onboarding, training, or ongoing enablement for customer-facing teams
  • Experience supporting customer success teams serving large enterprise customers
  • Experience building or improving an enablement program, service model, or governance framework
  • Experience working across regions and time zones within a global, matrixed organization
  • Familiarity with conversation intelligence, learning platforms, workflow automation, or applications of artificial intelligence in enablement

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Risk team builds trust, an essential ingredient for Stripe’s mission to increase the GDP of the internet. We make it possible for millions of businesses to access and use Stripe’s financial infrastructure while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader ecosystem from harm.

Risk sits at the center of our users’ and Stripe’s ability to grow safely. We help legitimate businesses access Stripe’s financial services, provide credit to creditworthy businesses, and increasingly help users manage their own risk. We also prevent fraud and financial crime, manage Stripe’s credit exposure, meet our obligations to regulators and financial partners, and enable Stripe’s product teams to launch and grow products safely. To do this, we set the policies and standards that guide how Stripe manages risk and develop the advanced AI, infrastructure, and product experiences that put them into practice for Stripe and our users.

At Stripe’s scale—$1.9 trillion in annual payment volume, equivalent to 1.6% of global GDP, processed across millions of businesses—we face risk problems no other company has encountered. The opportunities and complexities are only growing as AI reshapes what is possible, Stripe expands its product suite, regulators raise their expectations, and we support more businesses in more countries.

What you’ll do

As a Staff Product Manager on the Risk team, you will lead cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives that fundamentally change how Stripe and our users manage risk. You will identify the most important opportunities that cut across Risk’s infrastructure and products, define solutions to our most ambiguous problems, and drive execution from early technical shaping through delivery and adoption.

You will operate as a product counterpart to Risk’s senior technical leaders. You will shape infrastructure and product direction across Risk, connect work that would otherwise remain fragmented, and help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities. You will remain deeply engaged in the work, helping teams navigate difficult technical and product decisions.

Responsibilities

  • Identify high-leverage problems that cut across teams, turn ambiguity into clear product and technical direction, and establish measurable outcomes.
  • Lead major cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives from initial shaping through delivery, adoption, and iteration.
  • Lead changes in Risk’s approach to using data and AI to accurately identify and mitigate risk at scale.
  • Partner deeply with engineering, data science, and machine learning leaders to shape architecture, data foundations, models, APIs, and product experiences.
  • Help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities quickly and effectively while guiding Risk teams toward coherent, reusable infrastructure and product decisions.
  • Build alignment among teams with different goals and constraints, resolve difficult tradeoffs, and drive progress without relying on formal authority.

Who you are

We’re looking for an exceptional product leader who combines strong technical judgment with product insight, strategic range, and executional rigor. You identify important problems before they become obvious, bring clarity to deeply ambiguous spaces, and mobilize teams around solutions that work across products, organizations, and time horizons. You are deeply curious and stay at the forefront of advances in AI and technology, finding practical ways to apply them to our most challenging problems.

You move fluently from defining multi-year strategy to driving the details of execution. You build alignment and lead transformational work across teams without direct management authority. You earn trust through the clarity of your thinking, your focus on users, and your hands-on engagement in the work. You raise the ambition and effectiveness of the teams and product managers around you without needing to manage them.

Minimum requirements

  • A track record of identifying and delivering high-impact, transformational product or technical initiatives that span multiple teams and organizations.
  • Demonstrated ability to bring clarity to deeply ambiguous problems, set a compelling direction, and drive work through execution and adoption.
  • Strong technical judgment across data, machine learning, AI, APIs, platforms, and system architecture.
  • Experience partnering deeply with senior engineering, data science, and product leaders to shape both technical direction and product strategy.
  • Strong product judgment across foundational infrastructure and user-facing experiences, with a focus on building capabilities that solve real user problems.
  • Deep quantitative fluency and the ability to use data and causal reasoning to understand problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and measure outcomes.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders, build alignment across organizational boundaries, and drive execution without direct management authority.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate compelling strategies, influence technical and executive audiences, and make complex topics clear.
  • High agency, intellectual honesty, curiosity, and a low-ego, hands-on working style.

Preferred qualifications

  • An engineering background, preferably with a focus on machine learning.
  • Experience applying AI and machine learning to complex, high-stakes problems at scale.
  • Experience with fraud, credit, payments, financial services, trust and safety, or another domain involving complex decisions and asymmetric consequences.
  • Experience working with globally distributed teams.

About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like SBI, Money Forward, Paradigm, Dragonfly, Galaxy, and PayPal Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview

Mesh moves money across exchanges, wallets, banks, card networks and local payment rails. You will own that money: the right liquidity in the right place, partners pre-funded, settlements paid on time, corporate cash invested within policy, and every stuck transfer found and fixed. You also review the money-movement terms of new deals before they are signed, and you build, with Engineering and Product, the automation that tells us where liquidity is needed and moves it there.

What You'll Do

  • Manage daily cash and liquidity across bank accounts, customer fund accounts, custodians and stablecoin wallets, and forecast needs by product and corridor.
  • Run pre-funding and settlement lines with liquidity and payout partners: float levels, top-ups and line usage.
  • Work with Engineering and Product to build automated liquidity management for Mesh from Scratch (MFS), our new platform, from the ground up: real-time views of where liquidity is needed across bank accounts, wallets and partners, and automated deployment and rebalancing either internally or using an external tool. 
  • Review the money-movement terms of new customer and partner deals before signature: pre-funding, settlement timing, float, FX, subsidies and partner costs. Sign-off is required for ramp, OTC and other deals.
  • Track incentive and subsidy spend against approved limits.
  • Fund settlements with bank and partners on their cycles.
  • Work the daily exception queue: stuck or failed transfers, uncredited deposits and settlement breaks, resolved with partners and Engineering and logged with root cause.
  • Handle partner compliance requests such as source-of-funds reviews on large trades.
  • Invest corporate cash under a policy approved by the CEO & CFO.
  • Shape the investment policy and crypto signing matrix with the CFO, then run them along with approval limits and dual controls, and manage bank and custodian relationships.
  • Provide month-end statements and support for bank, investment, custody and restricted cash balances.
  • Maintain a 13-week cash forecast with Strategic Finance

Who You Are

  • 5+ years in treasury or payment operations at a payments company, money transmitter, exchange or stablecoin business.
  • Hands-on experience with both fiat and stablecoin money movement.
  • A deep understanding of the payments and liquidity space, and experience specifying and building automated treasury or liquidity systems with engineering teams.
  • Liquidity and prefunding management with external partners.
  • Experience reviewing settlement and funding terms in commercial contracts.
  • Experience operating under an investment policy and approval controls

Nice to have

  • Latin American payment rails (PIX, SPEI).

The compensation range provided may span multiple career levels and will be narrowed during the interview process based on factors including a candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location. For candidates outside of New York or San Francisco, compensation will be adjusted to reflect the applicable market and location-based pay band. The base salary range listed excludes commission (if applicable), equity, and benefits. The pay range represents the minimum and maximum target for new-hire compensation. Actual compensation may vary and may be higher or lower depending on individual circumstances.

Pay Range
$170,000—$210,000 USD

Why You’ll Love It Here

At Mesh, you're not stepping into a typical role—you're joining a rocket ship in mid-liftoff. You'll tackle complex, meaningful problems that actually move an industry forward, working alongside a sharp, motivated team that moves quickly, collaborates deeply, and expects everyone to operate with ownership. This is the kind of place where you'll see your work ship fast, make real impact, and be able to point to something and say, "I built that." You'll grow fast, level up your skills, and get a front-row seat to how a high-growth company scales from the inside, with competitive comp, solid benefits, and room to stretch your craft all coming standard. If you're energized by building, learning, and shaping something big—this is where you'll want to be.

In-Office Expectations

Employees based in our San Francisco, New York, and Bangalore hubs are expected to work from the office at least 40% of the time (approximately two days per week). This expectation may vary slightly depending on role, team, and business needs. Certain roles that require closer cross-functional collaboration or operational support may have additional in-office requirements, which will be discussed during the interview process. Our hybrid approach is designed to balance meaningful in-person collaboration, team building, and real-time decision-making with the flexibility to work remotely. We believe this structure supports strong execution while preserving autonomy and focus time.

How We Care For Our Team

We believe great work happens when people feel valued and supported. That starts with competitive salary and equity that grows as you and the company grow, plus comprehensive health coverage for you and your family. We offer unlimited PTO—and we mean it. Take the time you need to recharge and show up at your best.

We're invested in your growth with a dedicated budget for courses, conferences, and certifications. Work from wherever you're most productive with our remote-friendly approach, and count on having the top-tier tools and equipment you need to do exceptional work.

Mesh Pay is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

About the role

0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers.

Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes:

  • Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet

  • Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes

  • Kubernetes clusters and managed databases

  • A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps

All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs.

What you'll own

You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill.

  • Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses.

  • Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity.

  • Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades.

  • Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap.

  • Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps.

  • Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems.

  • Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet.

  • Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning.

  • Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform.

Our stack

Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies

Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering

Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery

Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi

CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries

Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor

Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging

Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall

AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations

Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust

Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka

Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking

Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access

Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud

Must-haves

  • We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines.

Kubernetes, in depth

  • Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions.

  • Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure.

  • Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work.

  • Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster.

  • Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables.

  • Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore.

  • Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux.

  • Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics.

CI/CD, in depth

  • Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates.

  • CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity.

  • Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing.

  • Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release.

  • Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection.

  • Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches.

  • Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets.

  • Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching.

Networking fundamentals

  • TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing.

  • DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups.

  • Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs.

  • Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs.

Also required

About the Role

We are seeking a Staff Full Stack Engineer to lead the technical direction of the team that builds Alpaca's Trading API product. Trading API serves developers, traders, and institutions who trade directly with Alpaca. The team owns that customer experience end to end: how customers access the platform, how their accounts are structured and secured, and the applications they use to trade.

The work spans the stack: customer-facing trading applications, the identity, account, and permission systems behind them, and integrations for partner apps and AI agents. The team also builds customer-facing trading features end to end, across our API.

This is a high-trust domain. These systems decide who can act on an account and what they are allowed to do. A defect can expose customer data, let the wrong person place a trade or move money, or lock a customer out at the moment they need to trade. The customer-facing surfaces also carry real-time trading: an order ticket or positions view that shows stale or wrong data can lead to a bad trade. We are looking for an engineer who has built and owned systems like this — identity and authorization, account models, and trading or financial applications — and who is as comfortable designing an authorization model as shipping the interface built on top of it.

You will not manage people directly. You will lead through architecture, code, design reviews, and mentorship, and you will remain a principal contributor. You will be the senior technical anchor for the team, partnering with the engineering manager, Product, and Design, and working closely with the trading, margin and risk, and platform teams behind the API.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for how customers access and use Trading API: identity and authentication, authorization and permissions, account and sub-account models, partner OAuth, and customer-facing trading and account-management applications.
  • Design the access model for increasingly complex account structures — multiple users per account, sub-accounts, entity and advisor accounts, and delegated API and agent access — so that permissions are explicit, auditable, and enforced on the server.
  • Lead technical delivery of next-generation Trading API customer applications, including real-time market data, order entry, and positions and order views, as the product expands to new customer surfaces.
  • Drive the move from legacy monolith endpoints to a dedicated application backend, with clear API contracts between customer applications and platform services such as trading, accounts, transfers, ledger, and market data.
  • Set the security bar for customer-facing systems: session and credential handling, MFA and passkeys, OAuth flows, rate limiting, input validation, and fast, durable responses to security findings.
  • Set the standard for safe delivery: feature flags, staged rollouts, preview environments, testing strategy, and production observability.
  • Partner with Product, Design, Compliance, Security, Brokerage Operations, and adjacent engineering teams to define behaviour and integration boundaries.
  • Lead design reviews, mentor senior and mid-level engineers, and raise the engineering bar as the team grows.
  • Act as a technical point of escalation for production issues on customer-facing Trading API systems, and drive durable prevention after incidents.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time on both backend services and customer-facing applications. Evidence of scope and ownership matters more than a strict year count.
  • Proven ownership of a production system where a defect could expose customer data, grant the wrong access, or cause financial loss.
  • Deep experience with authentication and authorization: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, session and token management, MFA, and role- or attribute-based permission models.
  • Strong backend expertise in Go, or deep experience in Java, Kotlin, C#, or Rust and a clear willingness to work primarily in Go.
  • Strong frontend experience with TypeScript and React, including complex, state-heavy applications. Experience with real-time data over WebSockets or other streaming protocols is strongly preferred.
  • Solid knowledge of relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred), API design (REST and gRPC), and service-oriented systems running on Kubernetes.

  • Track record of technical leadership and mentorship across teams. Product-minded: you care what the customer sees and why, and you are effective as a teammate.

  • Experience with identity platforms or building identity in-house (for example, Amazon Cognito, Keycloak, or Auth0), passkeys and WebAuthn, or delegated access for third-party applications.
  • Experience with API platforms and developer products: API keys, scopes, rate limits, SDKs, or developer dashboards.
  • Experience with agentic AI integrations, such as MCP servers or tooling that lets AI agents act safely on a user's behalf.
  • Familiarity with FIX or institutional trading workflows.
  • Experience leading migrations off a legacy monolith in production-critical environments.

About the job

We are seeking an Event Design Coordinator to manage the intake, production, and quality assurance of event-related creative requests coming from a wide range of teams across the business. This is a builder-and-gatekeeper role: you'll work hand-in-hand with designers to turn varied, often fast-turnaround requests into flawless deliverables, including booth graphics, signage, decks, digital assets, swag, and invites, while proactively spotting risks (timeline, brand, print spec, or logistical) before they become problems.

We are not looking for someone who simply routes tickets. We're looking for someone who understands both the creative process and the operational realities of live events well enough to catch a misaligned bleed line, a missing dieline, or a vendor deadline that's about to slip, and to fix it before anyone else notices.

Responsibilities

  • Request Intake & Triage

    • Serve as the primary point of contact for event-related creative requests coming from varied teams across Tether.

    • Scope each request clearly: deliverable type, format (print vs. digital), quantity, deadline, dimension, venue/vendor constraints, and brand requirements.

    • Flag conflicting timelines, unrealistic turnarounds, or missing information immediately, and propose a workable plan rather than waiting to be asked.

    Design Collaboration & Project Management

    • Brief designers with complete, unambiguous specs so work is right the first time.

    • Manage multiple concurrent event workstreams across different teams and deadlines without dropping details.

    • Track status across all active requests and proactively surface bottlenecks before they affect the event date.

    Quality Assurance (Print & Digital)

    • Review every designer deliverable before it goes back to the requesting team, checking brand consistency, copy accuracy, resolution, color mode (CMYK vs. RGB), bleed/trim/safe zones, file formats, and platform specs (e.g., booth panel dimensions, social crop ratios, slide aspect ratios).

    • Catch errors that would be costly or embarrassing to fix on-site or post-launch (typos, wrong sizing, low-res exports, broken links, outdated logos).

    • Maintain a QA checklist/process that scales across event types and gets sharper over time.

    Event Documentation & Knowledge Management

    • Document and file all assets, briefs, and final deliverables for each event in a shared drive, using a clear, consistent structure.

    • Organize files so the wider team can easily find past work, reuse assets, and cross-reference specs, timelines, or creative direction from previous events.

    • Keep a running record of vendor details, production specs, and lessons learned per event to speed up planning for future ones.

    Risk & Logistics Ownership

    • Anticipate what can go wrong, such as vendor lead times, print production windows, last-minute scope changes, and shipping delays, and build buffer and contingency plans into every project timeline.

    • Coordinate with vendors and print/production partners as needed to confirm specs and delivery windows.

    • Keep stakeholders across requesting teams and design aligned with clear, proactive status updates rather than reactive fire drills.

    Cross-Team Partnership

    • Act as a trusted liaison between business requesters and the design team, protecting designers' time from ambiguous briefs while protecting requesters from missed deadlines.

    • Continuously improve the intake and review process based on what goes wrong (or almost goes wrong) on each event.

  • 5+ years of experience in event marketing, event production, creative operations, or project management with a strong events component.

  • Proven experience managing print and digital production processes; you know what a dieline is, what "safe area" means, and why RGB assets can't go straight to print.

  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills: demonstrated ability to manage several concurrent, cross-functional requests with competing deadlines.

  • Sharp attention to detail, comfortable being the last line of defense before a deliverable ships.

  • Experience reviewing and giving actionable feedback on creative work from designers, without needing to be a designer yourself.

  • A proactive, risk-first mindset: you naturally ask "what could go wrong here?" and build a plan around the answer.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable managing stakeholders across different teams with different priorities.

  • Familiarity with project management tools (Asana, Monday, or similar) and design review tools like Figma

  • Experience setting up shared drive structures or asset libraries for teams.

  • Fluent in English and Spanish / Italian is a plus.

Important information for candidates
Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. To protect yourself, please keep the following in mind when applying for roles:

  • Apply only through our official channels. We do not use third-party platforms or agencies for recruitment unless clearly stated. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: https://tether.recruitee.com/

  • Verify the recruiter’s identity. All our recruiters have verified LinkedIn profiles. If you’re unsure, you can confirm their identity by checking their profile or contacting us through our website.

  • Be cautious of unusual communication methods. We do not conduct interviews over WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS. All communication is done through official company emails and platforms.

  • Double-check email addresses. All communication from us will come from emails ending in @tether.to or @tether.io

  • We will never request payment or financial details. If someone asks for personal financial information or payment at any point during the hiring process, it is a scam. Please report it immediately.

When in doubt, feel free to reach out through our official website.
